task_brief: This is day 5 of "Looking and Listening: Elements of Art and Sound". That is unit 1 in grade 3. Today is a second concept model about loud and soft. It takes about 40–60 minutes. It is one day's work, not the whole unit project. Your unit is working toward this: Create a small artwork and a short rhythm pattern that each use two elements explored this unit. Today helps by working on loud and soft. Your unit also covers line and shape, color, texture, and steady beat. Today is for practice. You are scored on finishing and being honest, not on getting it perfect.
primary_task: Look at a second artwork about loud and soft. Put it next to the first one. Name one choice both artists made the same. Name one place they are clearly different. Say what each difference does to the viewer or listener. Then make a small study using the second artist's way. Name both artworks. Anything you did not make must be free to use or properly credited. Use the attached Manuel Academy resource in this package. It gives you the model, example, or help sheet needed for this task. Keep today's work tied to your unit. Today is about loud and soft. It is part of "Looking and Listening: Elements of Art and Sound". Later days in this unit cover other things, like line and shape. Before you stop, do this check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about loud and soft; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. In grade 3 you need one clear try with a grown-up nearby. Say or write your reason in a sentence or two. Drawings, objects, or spoken answers are all fine.

sourceReference:
ATTACHED MANUEL ACADEMY LEARNER RESOURCE

Resource ID: ma-resource:ma-g3-arts-music-u01-l05

Lesson focus: loud and soft

Resource type: ACADEMY_ORIGINAL_MODEL

MODEL B — "Off-Centre Signal," contrasting with "Four-Step Signal." Pulse: 1 2 3 4 | 1 2 3 4. Rhythm: TA TI-TI rest TA | TI-TI TA-A TA. Optional pitches: C E D G | E D C C. Model A pauses at the bar line; Model B places silence inside the first group and lengthens a later event. Compare stability and surprise. Use it to study loud and soft; describe evidence before judging and adapt the example rather than copying a finished work.

How to use it: Use the attached Manuel Academy resource in this package. It gives you the model, example, or help sheet needed for this task.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.

task_accessibility_provisions: This task uses sound (loud and soft). You do not have to hear it to do it. You may use a written or drawn version, feel the beat by tapping or watching, or read the notes on paper instead.
Anything you have to study will also come as plain text, a described version, or a version you can touch.
You can take a break, stretch, or come back to this later. That does not lower your score.

Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.

The final product must remain the student’s own authorship; adult or AI assistance may support planning and feedback but must not create the graded work.

remediation: Reteaching for loud and soft follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for loud and soft, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for loud and soft works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of loud and soft, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking loud and soft mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply loud and soft under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on loud and soft rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
